children: Microsoft (MSFT) AI chief Mustafa Suleyman said "the race with China should not be used to delay safeguards for increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems," according to a Sept. 20 CNN interview.

Suleyman said U.S. developers can pursue advances while keeping people in control of AI systems. He also backed efforts to establish safety agreements and said the industry could benefit from practices developed in China.

His comments come as Washington debates the role of federal oversight. President Donald Trump has argued that the United States should maintain its lead over China in AI, while other technology leaders have called for additional safeguards. Reuters reported that AI safety and competition with China remain linked in upcoming U.S.-China discussions.

For Microsoft, broader AI rules could affect development and compliance costs across the industry. Alphabet (GOOG) and Meta Platforms (META) could also face similar considerations as they expand AI products. Microsoft recently published a proposed code of conduct focused on keeping AI systems responsive to human direction, including accepting correction and shutdown. The framework is open for public feedback.

title: Microsoft AI Chief Sends Stark Warning on AI Safety
